Convex hulls of groups of triangles

Source: R/tri_ops.R
tri_convex_hull.Rd

ST_ConvexHull() of the polygons the groups cover, from the triangles' vertices.

Usage

tri_convex_hull(x, group = NULL)

Arguments

x

A wkpool_tri.

group

Groups of triangles. Either one integer per triangle (a dense, 1-based group id, NA to leave a triangle out), or a data frame with columns triangle (row in x) and group, for groups that overlap (a triangle in several groups, as in an overlay). The default is the triangles' feature, or one group when the pool has no feature.

Value

A wk::wkb() vector of POLYGON, one per group id from 1 to the largest (POLYGON EMPTY for a group with fewer than three distinct points), with the pool's crs. Rings are counter-clockwise.

Examples

v <- data.frame(.vx = 1:6, x = c(0, 1, 1, 0, 2, 2), y = c(0, 0, 1, 1, 0, 1))
tri <- new_wkpool_tri(v, vx0 = c(1, 1, 2, 2), vx1 = c(2, 3, 5, 6),
                      vx2 = c(3, 4, 6, 3), feature = c(1, 1, 2, 2))
wk::as_wkt(tri_convex_hull(tri, rep(1L, 4)))
#> <wk_wkt[1]>
#> [1] POLYGON ((0 0, 2 0, 2 1, 0 1, 0 0))
